title: Must a product's check be kept from another product's data loaded in the same process?
description: The sealed engine keeps a check's query from files, web addresses, extensions and settings, but one engine serves every product a process loads. In a long-running process that holds two products at once (the app's server, the agent tools, the desktop app) a product's check can name another product's loaded data and read it, though never change it; the check of a repo loads its products one after another, so a gate that runs it is not exposed. Options: (a) accept it, as the products of one process share an owner and a repo; (b) one engine per product, which keeps each product's data apart at the cost of a schema copy and more memory per product; (c) a list of the loaded data sets a check may name, held by Lathe before the query runs, which a parse of the query can enforce but which is a second rule beside the engine's own.

title: Split the four aggregates that hold more than 15 use cases?
description: A use case sits with its result's aggregate or read model, so a domain's use cases are counted per group. Four aggregates hold more than max_children (15): Domain (21), Use case (21), Aggregate (19) and Read model (16), each Add, Change, Remove and Move for five or six entities. The product accepts these four too-many-children warnings (accepted warnings 12 to 16) until the Owner decides whether to split them: for example Term, Domain service and Repository out of Domain, or Flow and UC requirement out of Use case. Splitting an aggregate is an essential domain-model change, and the limit is never raised.

title: What marks a domain as a platform domain, so the nav lists it under Shared?
description: The nav lists Health, Domains and Shared, and Shared is meant to hold the platform domain (shared plumbing, such as Platform) before the Shared folder. Nothing in a product's data marks a domain as a platform: Platform's subdomain type is supporting, as Checking's is, and a match on its name is no rule. Until it is marked, every domain is listed under Domains and Shared holds the Shared folder alone. Options: (a) a platform subdomain type, or a yes/no field on the domain, a schema change every product gets; (b) list the generic domains under Shared, with Platform marked generic, though Platform is specific to Lathe rather than solved the same way everywhere; (c) keep every domain under Domains, with Platform last by its position.
